observations: fabro-bde4 basis verified fresh (incident 2026-09-07, PR #33 in git log); wait.rs has only terminal/merged/closed_unmerged/timeout — gap real.
Spec ambiguity resolved in brief: value named `blocked`, signal = pulls-API mergeable_state dirty/blocked sustained 2 consecutive polls (10s GitHub poll interval in wait.rs), no checks-API addition.
TS client regen needs java (fabro-3b1b open): brief permits consistent hand-edit of the generated client if openapi-generator-cli unavailable.
Conductor until=merged routing lives in TWO prompt files: merge-leg.md (step 4) and develop-leg.md (step 5) — both must gain the blocked route; revise-leg.md is until=terminal only.

painpoints.text: TestAppStateBuilder (lib/apps/fabro-server/src/test_support.rs) had no github_api_base_url setter until this seed added one — every it-test needing a mock GitHub had to either stay in the cfg(test) unit suite or duplicate create_github_token_app_state (fabro-bde4, run 01M1XN2KWG6T0PHRTJWZ8R0AZX). Suggestion: consider exposing a shared mock-github app helper in test_support so future it-tests don't re-derive the token-strategy settings + vault_entries incantation.

observations: httpmock 0.8.3 has no per-mock hit limit (no up_to_n_times); modeling transient-then-changed GitHub responses requires spawning the request task, waiting on mock.calls_async(), then mock.delete() + creating the follow-up mock — the pattern used in merged_wait_ignores_transient_blocked_observation.

wait.rs uses std::time::Instant for the poll cadence, so paused-clock tokio tests cannot fast-forward it; the confirmation interval (BLOCKED_CONFIRMATION_POLL_INTERVAL=1.5s) is what keeps sustained-window tests fast rather than 10s+ (GITHUB_POLL_INTERVAL).

painpoints.text: scripts/qualitygate.nu runs `cargo nextest -p <touched-crates>` without ever building the fabro CLI bin, while fabro-server's SVG render handler tests require target/debug/fabro — any run touching fabro-server in a cold sandbox deterministically fails the gate on 3 render tests (observed run 01M1XN2KWG6T0PHRTJWZ8R0AZX tester, ~186 KB output). I fixed the test side (skip when unresolvable), but a gate-side option would be a `cargo build -p fabro-cli --bin fabro` precondition when fabro-server is in the touched set, keeping real-path coverage in run sandboxes too.

observations: The render-exe fallback spawned the test binary itself with `__render-graph`, which libtest interprets as a filter — the failure masqueraded as an HTTP 500 'protocol violation' rather than an obvious missing-binary error, costing a diagnosis cycle; the new explicit SpawnFailed message in lib/apps/fabro-server/src/server/handler/graph.rs makes this class self-explanatory.
